content:
Temperature is the Class 5 chapter students underestimate — Celsius-Fahrenheit conversions and change-through-zero questions catch the unprepared. Here is what the IMO Class 5 temperature chapter tests, with a free 10-question test.

What the Class 5 Maths Olympiad Temperature chapter tests

  • Reading thermometers in °C and °F
  • Conversions: °F = 9C/5 + 32 and back
  • Temperature rise, fall and differences (through negatives)
  • Benchmark temperatures (freezing, body, boiling)

Key facts your child should know

  • Water freezes at 0°C / 32°F and boils at 100°C / 212°F.
  • Body temperature ≈ 37°C = 98.6°F.
  • °F = (9/5 × °C) + 32; °C = 5/9 × (°F − 32).
  • From −4° a rise of 10° reaches 6° — count through zero.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding 32 before multiplying by 9/5.
  • Sign slips on temperatures below zero.
  • Confusing a temperature with a temperature difference.

quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: Tea served at 85 °C cools down to 31 °C. Through how many degrees does it cool?
The average temperature over three days was 20 °C. The first two days recorded 18 °C and 19 °C. What was the temperature on the third day?
The temperature falls steadily by 2 °C every hour. If it is 30 °C now, what will it be after 5 hours?
During a cold wave the temperature in a valley was 4 °C at 9 pm. It fell by 11 °C by 4 am. What was the temperature at 4 am?
The temperature at a hill station was 6 °C at 6 pm. It dropped 2 °C every hour. At what time did it reach 0 °C?
questions.explanation: A drop of 6 °C is needed; at 2 °C per hour that takes 3 hours: 6 pm + 3 h = 9 pm.

faq.q: How much did the temperature change from −4°C to 6°C?
faq.a: It rose 10 degrees — 4 degrees to reach zero and 6 more above it.
